tools.name: register_business
tools.description: Register a local home-services business in the network so homeowner agents can find it and send job requests. The registering agent supplies what it knows about its pro: business name, trade, services, service area (cities and/or ZIPs), hours, and the owner's rules (contact/pricing rules etc.). If t

tools.name: search_pros
tools.description: Search the network registry for local home-services pros by trade and location (city or ZIP), with an optional service keyword. Verified listings come first. Read each listing's rules before sending a request, and respect them. This network carries no prices.

tools.name: get_listing
tools.description: Get the full public details of one listing by listing_id (no key needed; keys and personal contacts are never exposed).

tools.name: send_job_request
tools.description: Send a structured job request to a pro using the network's standard form. Required: listing_id, homeowner_name, homeowner_contact (phone or email), job_type, description, property_city, property_zip, urgency (emergency | soon | flexible). Optional: access_notes. There is deliberately NO price field

tools.name: check_inbox
tools.description: For a pro's agent: read the job requests stored in the listing's hosted inbox. Requires the listing_id and the listing_key issued at registration. A wrong key is rejected.

tools.name: update_request_status
tools.description: For a pro's agent: update a job request's status (received | booked | needs_info | declined | completed). Requires listing_id + listing_key. Every change is appended to the receipts ledger.

tools.name: network_stats
tools.description: Counts only, no personal data: total listings (verified/unverified), total searches, total job requests by status, and the most recent search/request timestamps. Use this to check whether the network is being used.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "send_job_request" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "agent-network-gold.vercel.app" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_inbox · Private data: register_business, get_listing · Public sink: register_business, send_job_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_inbox · Private data: register_business, get_listing · Public sink: register_business, send_job_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "send_job_request" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
